findings.evidence: In `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go`, `buildWith` overwrites `b.nameMapCTE = make(map[string]struct{})` and fills it from `w.CTEs`. While building those CTEs, `buildWith` calls `buildCte` -> `buildResultSetNode(cte.Query.Query, true)`, which can run `buildSelect`/`buildSetOpr` and call `buildWith` again for nested WITH, overwriting `b.nameMapCTE` with the inner names; there is no save/restore. `buildUpdate` later uses `if _, ok := b.nameMapCTE[t.Name.L]; !ok { appendVisitInfo(... mysql.SelectPriv, dbName, t.Name.L, ...) }`, so a nested WITH can clobber the outer CTE-name set and cause the outer CTE table to be added to privilege checks again.
findings.fix: Make the UPDATE-side CTE filter scoped and non-clobberable: compute a local `map[string]struct{}` from `update.With.CTEs` inside `buildUpdate` (instead of relying on a shared mutable field), or implement a proper stack/save-restore mechanism for `nameMapCTE` so nested `buildWith()` calls don't overwrite the map needed by `buildUpdate`. Optionally gate the skip by `t.Schema.L == ""` to only treat unqualified names as CTE candidates.
findings.impact: For UPDATE statements using CTEs where any CTE definition contains a nested WITH, `buildUpdate` can regress to appending a `mysql.SelectPriv` check for the CTE table name. In sessions without a current DB (common when using fully-qualified base table names), this can reproduce the original privilege-check failure the PR intends to fix (the CTE table has empty schema, so dbName resolves from an empty CurrentDB and `pm.RequestVerification` fails).
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd): `buildWith` still overwrites `b.nameMapCTE` without save/restore and `buildUpdate` still consults it to skip privilege entries; no later fix found.
findings.verify: Add a regression case with nested WITH inside a CTE definition + UPDATE join executed with no CurrentDB: e.g. connect without default DB, `WITH outer AS (WITH inner AS (SELECT ...) SELECT ... FROM inner) UPDATE db.t JOIN outer ...` should succeed for a user granted needed privileges on `db.*`, and should not require any privilege on the CTE name itself.
findings.what: `PlanBuilder.nameMapCTE` is a single mutable field and not scoped/stacked; nested `WITH` inside a CTE definition can overwrite it, so `buildUpdate` may fail to recognize the UPDATE statement's own CTE table names and wrongly add `mysql.SelectPriv` visitInfo entries for them again.

subject: planner/core: fix a wrong privilege check for CTE & UPDATE statement (#57430)
summary: This commit fixes the reported UPDATE+CTE privilege issue by skipping SELECT-privilege `visitInfo` entries for CTE table names (tracked via `PlanBuilder.nameMapCTE`). However, `nameMapCTE` is overwritten on every `buildWith()` call and is not restored across nested WITH construction, so nested WITH inside CTE definitions can clobber the map and reintroduce the wrong privilege check for UPDATE statements in those cases.
